Pre-trial calibration of the stress test

Source: R/calibrate.R
stress_calibrate.Rd

Simulates trials from a planned design and runs a light stress test on each (covariance, inference, covariate, weighting and leave-one-out families, plus the greedy deletion search if fragility = TRUE), so that a sponsor can see, before unblinding, how often a trial of this design would be classed robust, sensitive or fragile at each power, and how often the marginal flag would be set.

Usage

stress_calibrate(
  n_per_arm = 50,
  power = c(0, 0.5, 0.8, 0.95),
  n_trials = 100,
  n_visits = 4,
  sigma = 10,
  rho = 0.6,
  dropout = 0.08,
  baseline_beta = 0.5,
  errors = "normal",
  t_df = 3,
  hetero = 1,
  mnar = 0,
  interaction = 0,
  fragility = FALSE,
  cores = 1L,
  seed = 1,
  rule = c("interval", "interval_or_direction")
)

Arguments

n_per_arm

Subjects per arm.

power

Target powers for the pre-specified analysis; the effect size giving each is derived from the design (0 gives the null).

n_trials

Trials per power.

n_visits

Number of post-baseline visits.

sigma

Residual standard deviation at each visit.

rho

AR(1) correlation between adjacent visits.

dropout

Baseline per-visit dropout probability.

baseline_beta

Slope of the response on the baseline covariate.

errors, t_df, hetero, mnar, interaction

Misspecification settings passed to simulate_trial().

fragility

Run the deletion search (slower).

cores

Worker processes (the trials are distributed, so each trial's families run on one core).

seed

Base seed.

rule

Classification rule for stress_verdict().

Value

A data frame of class stress_calibration with one row per power: the effect size, observed power, and the proportion of trials with each verdict, the marginal flag, and (if run) a one-subject fragility; attr(, "trials") holds the per-trial rows.

Examples

stress_calibrate(n_per_arm = 20, power = c(0, 0.8), n_trials = 2)
#> Stress-test calibration: 20 per arm, 4 visits, SD 10, AR(1) 0.6, dropout 0.08 per visit
#>  power_target delta trials power_observed marginal robust sensitive fragile
#>           0.0  0.00      2            0.0        0      1         0       0
#>           0.8  8.98      2            0.5        0      1         0       0
#>  sensitive_given_sig fragile_k1_given_sig
#>                   NA                   NA
#>                    0                   NA
